question: Last Sunday, Acayro Sánchez, the presiding judge in many cases into urban planning corruption, who was himself subsequently convicted following a complaint from the lawyers of some of the plaintiffs, was interviewed on the Spanish TV network LaSexta’s programme ‘Salvados’1.

The complaint, received and heard at first instance by a magistrate with whom Acayro had competed for the presidency of the High Court of Justice of Cantabria, resulted in his conviction. The Supreme Court subsequently increased the sentence and struck him off. The judgement2 included dissenting opinions which stated that established facts of the case had been altered3.
The judges who rendered the judgement and the prosecutor both have links with a particular political party. The proceedings lasted from 2021 to 2026. Questions for the Commission: 1.
Is the fact of a judge trying another judge with whom they have a pending legal dispute compatible with European standards for judicial impartiality?
Is the court of last instance altering established facts to the detriment of the defendant without a hearing compatible with the right to a fair trial?
What does the Commission intend to do to address excessive procedural delays and ensure that such proceedings are of a reasonable duration?
